ca_emerald_city_2.blurb: Emerald City is a small crag in the OZ area of Joshua Tree National Park, tucked into a side canyon beyond the Poppie Field Boulders. It has eight routes, mostly short trad lines, with two bolted face climbs and one aid line. Free grades run from 5.8 up to 5.11, with several of the harder ones in the 5.11 range. The monzogranite is brown and broken by cracks and face features, so there is room for both jamming and thin slab moves. The walk up the wash from the northern trailhead is a long one, close to an hour, which makes this a full-day objective.

ca_bunny_slopes.blurb: Bunny Slopes is a slab crag beside Tioga Road in Tuolumne Meadows, Yosemite National Park. It has eight routes on granodiorite, with lines reaching around 165 feet. Most are trad or slab routes with bolts at 5.6 and 5.7, with a single 5.8 and a 5.9 on top of them, so it suits climbers stepping onto Tuolumne's friction and knob terrain. One route is a bolted sport line. The walk from the road is only about five minutes, which makes it a convenient stop when the bigger domes are a commitment.

ca_2_robinson.blurb: Robinson is a small sector of the Silver Lake crag on the June Lake Loop in the Eastern Sierra. The sound, compact quartzite holds eight routes: four top-ropes, two sport lines and two trad climbs. The steeper upper part of the cliff is only 30 to 45 feet tall, and the ground below it is mostly scrambling rather than sustained climbing. Grades start at scrambling level and top out at 5.8, with three routes at that grade. The top can be reached by an easy fourth-class gully, which suits top-rope setups.

ca_dog_wall.blurb: Dog Wall is a short, multi-coloured craglet just upstream of the Horseshoe Piles, above Horseshoe Lake in the Eastern Sierra. It has eight routes mixing top-rope, trad, alpine-style and sport lines, with grades from 5.8 to 5.12 and the bulk around 5.10. The wall faces northeast and sits in afternoon shade, with a creek and wildflowers alongside, though mosquitoes can be a nuisance early in the season. Many lines can be top-roped from an anchor reached by walking above, while a few finish with a walk-off or a single-bolt rappel. The uphill walk from the piles takes about fifteen minutes.

ca_lower_dinosaur_rock_w_face.blurb: This is one side of Lower Dinosaur Rock, one of the formations along Keller Peak Road in the San Bernardino Mountains near Running Springs, set among pines. It has eight routes: seven trad and one sport. Most are moderate cracks, with one harder bolted face line at 5.11, and the grades span 5.8 to 5.11 with 5.10 the most common. The rock is very sharp, so tape is worth bringing for the crack climbs. This side sees less traffic than the rest of the formation.
ca_lower_dinosaur_rock_w_face.approach: A well-used trail leaves from the edge of Campsite 2 on Keller Peak Road and reaches the rock in roughly 5 to 10 minutes.

ca_lower_tier_2.blurb: Lower Tier is a small wall on Trapper Dome, on the western slope of the southern Sierra Nevada. It has eight routes, split evenly between sport and trad, mostly face climbing with a few cracks. Grades run from 5.8 to 5.10, and five of the eight are in the 5.10 range. The Upper Tier is reached by continuing along the base of the dome, so the two are easily combined in one outing. The walk from the road is only a few minutes.
ca_lower_tier_2.parking_note: Several roadside pull-outs, mostly on the right-hand side as you drive in, put you within a few minutes' walk of the slabs.
ca_lower_tier_2.approach: No formal trail. Walk from the pull-out to the slabs and follow the foot of the dome along the base of the wall.

ca_1_croft.blurb: Croft is the first numbered sector of the Silver Lake crag on the June Lake Loop in the Eastern Sierra. All eight routes are top-ropes on sound quartzite. A grassy ramp running diagonally across the cliff divides it into two parts: a low slab with positive holds and moderate moves, and a steeper upper section roughly 60 to 80 feet tall, with the tallest slice reaching about 175 feet. Grades run from scrambling level to 5.9, with 5.8 the most common. The walk from the parking lot to the base takes roughly 5 to 13 minutes, depending on which part you head for.

ca_boy_and_girl_rocks.blurb: Boy and Girl Rocks are a pair of granodiorite boulders in the Buttermilks Main area near Bishop, just downhill of Pope's Hat. There are eight problems, ranging from VB up to V5, with the bulk at V0 and V1, so it works as a warm-up stop for the main hillside. Girl Rock has a low, heavily chalked overhang with a lot of patina, and Boy Rock sits a few feet further downhill. Expect the usual Buttermilks mix of patina, jugs and sharp crimps, with flat, sandy landings.
